original_question: Which rational linear combinations of Hodge numbers and Chern characteristic numbers of a smooth complex projective variety are topological invariants, under oriented or unoriented homeomorphism or diffeomorphism, and which are not?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 31 ("Topological invariance of characteristic numbers of algebraic varieties"), together with the quoted classification answer immediately following it (cf. [KS13, Theorem 4]).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right problem family: rational linear combinations, Hodge numbers together with Chern characteristic numbers, smooth complex projective varieties, and the need to distinguish invariance under oriented versus unoriented homeomorphisms or diffeomorphisms. It is also aligned with the nearby context in Section 7, where Kotschick explains that "topological invariant" must be interpreted in exactly those senses before giving the final classification.
missing_details: The paper's problem is naturally dimension-by-dimension: one should quantify over smooth complex projective n-folds X for each fixed complex dimension n.
In the oriented cases, the relevant orientation is the preferred complex orientation on the underlying manifold.
The paper's final classification is not just a loose list of invariants; it is an if-and-only-if statement.
The exact classification uses Betti numbers and Pontryagin numbers: these must appear explicitly in a fully stand-alone formulation.
The mixed Hodge-Chern statement is only true modulo the universal Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch relations; equivalently one may add suitable linear combinations of chi_p - Td_p.
The notation chi_p should be defined explicitly as chi_p(X) = sum_q (-1)^q h^{p,q}(X).
The notation Td_p should be identified as the Todd-genus/Todd-polynomial characteristic number corresponding to chi_p via Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch.
There is a paper-critical exception: the unoriented diffeomorphism classification must exclude complex dimension 2.
If one phrases the statement in the Hodge-ring language of [KS13], one should note that Hodge numbers are understood modulo the universal Kahler symmetries h^{p,q} = h^{q,p} = h^{n-p,n-q}.
Your wording says "which are not," but the paper gives a complete classification, so the complement is simply every rational linear combination not falling into the listed classes.
refined_question: For each complex dimension n, classify all Q-linear combinations of the Hodge numbers h^{p,q}(X) and Chern characteristic numbers of smooth complex projective n-folds X that depend only on the underlying manifold, distinguishing the four notions of invariance: oriented homeomorphism, oriented diffeomorphism, unoriented homeomorphism, and unoriented diffeomorphism.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, modulo the universal Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch relations chi_p(X) = Td_p(X) (that is, after possibly adding suitable Q-linear combinations of chi_p - Td_p, where chi_p(X) = sum_q (-1)^q h^{p,q}(X)), are the oriented homeomorphism/diffeomorphism invariants exactly the Q-linear combinations of Betti and Pontryagin numbers, and are the unoriented homeomorphism invariants in every dimension, together with the unoriented diffeomorphism invariants for n != 2, exactly the Q-linear combinations of Betti numbers?
justification: The draft is aiming at Hirzebruch's Problem 31 as updated in Section 7 of Kotschick's paper. Problem 31 asks for the topological invariance of h^{p,q} and Chern characteristic numbers and for the determination of all invariant linear combinations. The nearby context then sharpens the ambiguous phrase "topological invariant" into homeomorphism versus diffeomorphism and orientation-preserving versus orientation-forgetting versions, and the section concludes by quoting the complete solution from [KS13, Theorem 4]. To make the question fully stand-alone and faithful to that solution, one must state it for each fixed complex dimension, include the preferred complex orientation in the oriented cases, and make explicit that the answer is only well-posed up to the universal Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch relations chi_p = Td_p. The refined version stays close to the original intent of Problem 31 while incorporating exactly the distinctions and exception actually used in the paper, especially the exclusion of complex dimension 2 in the unoriented diffeomorphism case.
